note: dopamine + neutral sulfuric acid (5 heavy atoms: S+4O, no carbon). Whether H2SO4 is auto-stripped depends on the not-yet-fixed N threshold in the no-carbon/<=N-heavy-atom heuristic (RFC section 6, open question). Held out specifically to NOT let this fixture's expected answer silently fix N's value during rule design -- the implementation round must decide N (or add a small named always-strip set of common mineral-acid/polyatomic-counterion fragments) and then check this case, not the reverse.

CORRECTED after implementation (the original fixture note had an arithmetic error): phosphoric acid is P+4*O = 5 heavy atoms, not 4 -- it is NOT a boundary case at N=4, it sits in the same over-threshold bucket as H2SO4 (holdout-01). Unlike holdout-01, ethanolamine (NCCO, 4 heavy atoms) is smaller than phosphoric acid here, so a pure heavy-atom-count policy with no named-acid recognition keeps the acid over the amine. This is a genuine, disclosed limitation of the Phase 1 default policy (see RFC section 6), verified via the implementation's own test suite (crates/chematic-chem/src/standardize.rs, phase1_holdout_02_phosphoric_acid_outranks_small_amine_disclosed_gap) -- not the boundary-value question this fixture was originally designed to probe.

calcium diacetate. Ca2+ is NOT on this RFC's default always-strip list (Na/K/Li/Cl/Br/I/F only). Under the structural no-carbon heuristic it still classifies as salt (1 heavy atom, no carbon), so the expected fragment-selection OUTCOME is unaffected either way here -- held out to check that whichever mechanism handles it (always-strip list vs. general heuristic), the AUDIT LOG's stated rule_id differs accordingly and isn't reported as 'monatomic_always_strip_ion' if Ca2+ was never added to that literal list.
lithium acetate; Li+ IS on the default always-strip list per the RFC text but untested by any main-fixture row -- holdout coverage check, not a design-driving case
